role: Risk-department review of one appointed oil strategy, followed by investment-decision-committee approval of a strategy risk mandate and an independently chosen capital authorization.
invariants: the risk department proposes strategy capacity, volatility, drawdown, concentration, liquidity and roll limits but does not allocate company capital
the investment decision committee approves the strategy risk mandate and independently sets capital authorization
capital authorization can differ from the risk department advisory capital recommendation but cannot exceed available company equity in the current unlevered allocation contract
the strategy director's capital deployment preference applies only inside committee-authorized capital
capital deployment changes the PM strategy-intent envelope but is not an input to the risk policy, risk recommendation or committee authorization
PM strategy intent and strategy-risk limits are parallel quantities anchored independently to authorized capital; they are compared by clipping and are never multiplied into a serial haircut chain
strategy risk can preserve or shrink strategy intent but cannot create a direction, enlarge intent or cross through zero
company risk is applied after strategy risk and market hard limits remain final
all volatility, liquidity and drawdown inputs are visible at the decision cutoff
the same strategy profile, risk profile, committee approval and visible state produce the same review, mandate and result
the layer never writes back to market, forecast, macro, volume or open interest
